title: The Phone Features I Can't Believe We Don't Have
excerpt: Short post, I've just had these ideas bouncing in my head for a while and it keeps annoying me phones have never implemented them. First is a "guest lock"...
content_html:
14 Aug, 2026

Short post, I've just had these ideas bouncing in my head for a while and it keeps annoying me phones have never implemented them.

First is a "guest lock". There's a better name for it somewhere but it's not my job to find it. Android and iOS should have a system-level ability to lock focus on the active application. This would mean you could open a concert ticket, a photo, or your digital insurance record (which is a VERY BAD IDEA to hand to a cop without this feature), guest-lock your phone, and hand it over without any worry that someone could start opening other apps to look for things you didn't want to show them.

The UX would be simple; inputting any command that would unfocus the current app would present a standard system unlock prompt. This means it would be more easily abused if you're using biometric unlocks, yes, but by no means does it make the feature useless. And it normalizes a level of trust between individuals which is appropriate, but impossible, in many situations.

A really nice feature would be a hardware button triggering this mode! Imagine how easy that would be to hand over your phone with vanishingly little worry that it could be abused.

You'll notice I mentioned showing a photo earlier. Obviously, the standard guest lock implementation doesn't prevent someone from scrolling your entire camera roll. A really good implementation would support specific locking features, such as setting a range of allowed photos, beyond which the guest user can't scroll. But that increases friction a lot, and leads to my second idea.

The second thing I would like is some form of hiding images from browsing in the camera roll. This could mean marking certain images as requiring a privileged viewing mode, or else they're completely hidden. Or it could mean defining "sets", which could be hidden as a group, or could hook into the above guest lock feature, or even other system features like mass-uploading. I bet there are other ways this could work, too.

If the need for this latter feature isn't obvious to you, well, that's ok. It would be very useful to me.

content_html_zh:
14 Aug, 2026

简短的帖子，这些想法在我脑海中闪现了一段时间，这让我很恼火，手机从未实现过它们。

首先是“宾客锁”。 在某个地方有一个更好的名字，但找到它不是我的工作。 Android 和 iOS 应该具有系统级能力来锁定活动应用程序的焦点。 这意味着您可以打开一张音乐会门票、一张照片或您的数字保险记录（如果没有此功能，将其交给警察是一个非常糟糕的主意），来宾锁定您的手机，然后将其交给您，而不必担心有人可能会开始打开其他应用程序来查找您不想向他们展示的内容。

用户体验会很简单；输入任何会取消当前应用程序焦点的命令都会出现标准系统解锁提示。 这意味着如果您使用生物识别解锁，它会更容易被滥用，是的，但这绝不会让该功能变得无用。 它使个人之间的信任水平正常化，这在许多情况下是适当的，但不可能。

一个非常好的功能是触发此模式的硬件按钮！ 想象一下，交出你的手机是多么容易，而且几乎不用担心它会被滥用。

你会注意到我之前提到过展示一张照片。 显然，标准的访客锁实现并不能阻止某人滚动您的整个相机胶卷。 一个真正好的实现将支持特定的锁定功能，例如设置允许的照片范围，超出该范围来宾用户将无法滚动。 但这会增加很多摩擦，并引出了我的第二个想法。

我想要的第二件事是以某种形式隐藏相机胶卷中的图像。 这可能意味着将某些图像标记为需要特权查看模式，否则它们将被完全隐藏。 或者它可能意味着定义“集合”，它可以作为一个组隐藏，或者可以连接到上述访客锁定功能，甚至其他系统功能，例如批量上传。 我敢打赌还有其他方法可以实现这一点。

如果您对后一个功能的需求并不明显，那也没关系。 这对我来说非常有用。
